blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it

findings.evidence:
export const bucket = (ps: Price[]) =>
  ps.reduce<Record<string, Price[]>>((a, p) => ((a[(p.cents >> 4) & 0x3e8 ? "hi" : "lo"] ||= []).push(p), a), {});
findings.recommendation: A developer who has not read the proposal cannot tell from this line where "premium" starts: the threshold is hidden behind a shift and a hex mask (`(p.cents >> 4) & 0x3e8`), with no named constant and no comment; the reduce relies on the comma operator and `||=` inside an index expression; the names `ps`, `a`, `p`, `bucket` and the untyped string keys `"hi"` / `"lo"` say nothing about cheap versus premium. A reader is likely to misread the condition as "1000 cents or more" (0x3e8 is 1000) — and it is not: 500 cents gives `(500 >> 4) & 0x3e8 === 8`, so a 5-euro product lands in "hi", which the shape of the line hides (correctness itself is the developer's to confirm). Write it plainly: a named constant `PREMIUM_THRESHOLD_CENTS = 1000` ("10 euros", from the proposal), a named function such as `splitByPriceBand(prices)` returning `{ cheap: Price[]; premium: Price[] }`, built with two `filter` calls or a `for … of` loop on `price.cents >= PREMIUM_THRESHOLD_CENTS`.
findings.title: `bucket` packs the premium rule into an unreadable bit-twiddling one-liner
